Pre-crash movement through telematics data shows the Lucid vehicle proceeding straight driving 80 mph Eastbound in lane 1 on [XXX] (speed limit is 45 mph) on [XXX], 2023. Initial information indicated one or both vehicles were towed away, though no information was included about injuries. A second before impact, the driver applies the brake pedal and provides steering wheel input to the right, then to the left, and finally to the right before impact. The telematics data shows the vehicle heading East on [XXX] and the crash signal occurs in the Northeast corner of the [XXX] exit ([XXX], [XXX]), the speed of the Lucid Vehicle is logged at 53mph. Telematics data shows the driver airbag deployed.  On [XXX], a conversation with the towing company employee occurred in which the employee stated that the Lucid vehicle was cut off by an oncoming vehicle, a Chevy Crew Cab Pickup truck heading Westbound on [XXX]. The truck was turning left onto [XXX]. and the Lucid vehicle impacted the rear right of the truck. The towing company employee stated that people involved in the accident were transported to the hospital for medical treatment.

On March [XXX], 2025 at 12:11 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a remote controlled robot on [XXX] near [XXX]. 
The Waymo AV was traveling northwest on [XXX]  when a personal remote controlled toy robot entered the roadway from between a row of bikes on a bike rack on the right-hand side of [XXX], and the front of the Waymo AV made contact with the remote controlled robot. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The robot sustained damage.
Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 2 of Standing General Order 2021-01. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On April [XXX], 2026 at 9:44 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on [XXX] near [XXX]. 

The Waymo AV was traveling southeastbound on a narrow portion of [XXX], with vehicles parked at the curb in both directions, in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV transitioned to manual mode and the test driver continued proceeding forward on a curve of [XXX] where the roadway continued to the left, and the front right side of the Waymo AV made contact with the rear left side of a passenger car parked facing southeast at the curb. As a result of this collision, the passenger car was pushed forward, and the front of the passenger car made contact with the rear of a second passenger car parked directly in front of the first passenger car. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. All three vehicles sustained damage.

Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because a vehicle involved was towed away. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On October [XXX], 2024 at 3:58 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on [XXX] at [XXX]. 
The Waymo AV was traveling south in the left lane on [XXX] and came to a stop in a queue of traffic for the red traffic light at the intersection with [XXX]. As the Waymo AV approached the intersection and came to a stop, a passenger car which was following behind the Waymo AV at a low rate of speed approached the Waymo AV from behind and partially crossed into the right-hand travel lane. The passenger car continued proceeding slowly forward until the front of the passenger car made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. After contact occurred, the passenger car remained in contact with the rear of the Waymo AV, and several bystanders approached the passenger car, attempting to communicate with the driver. Once the traffic light turned green, the Waymo AV proceeded through the intersection and pulled over at the curb on the south side of the intersection to avoid obstructing other traffic. While the Waymo AV proceeded through the intersection, the passenger car continued to roll forward into the intersection, and was stopped by several bystanders. Law enforcement communicated to Waymo that the driver of the passenger car was experiencing a medical emergency and was transported from the scene in an ambulance. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.
Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On December [XXX], 2024 at 1:08 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (Waymo AV) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck on [XXX] at [XXX].
The Waymo AV was in autonomous mode traveling north in the rightmost of two lanes on [XXX] when it partially entered the left adjacent lane to make room for a cyclist on its right who was traveling in the same direction. A heavy truck behind in the left adjacent lane proceeded forward, and the Waymo AV test driver transitioned to manual mode immediately before the rear driver side of the Waymo AV made contact with the front passenger side of the heavy truck. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AVs Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.
Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because a vulnerable road user influenced the driving task of a vehicle involved and a vehicle involved was towed away. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On February [XXX], 2025 at 1:39 PM MT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Phoenix, Arizona was in a collision involving a passenger car on [XXX]. 
The Waymo AV was traveling eastbound on[XXX] in the dedicated left turn lane preparing to make an unprotected left turn onto [XXX] when it came to a stop behind a passenger car also waiting to make an unprotected left turn. While the Waymo AV remained stopped, the passenger car proceeded to make an unprotected left turn onto [XXX], crossing in front of an oncoming SUV traveling west on[XXX]. The passenger car was struck on its passenger side by the oncoming SUV, causing the passenger car to rotate counter-clockwise. After impact, the passenger car then continued turning left, circling back towards the Waymo AV. The front passenger side of the passenger car then made contact with the front driver side of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage. A passenger in the Waymo AV and the driver of the passenger car were transported to the hospital from the scene in an ambulance.
Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 1 of Standing General Order 2021-01 because an individual involved was transported from the scene to a hospital for medical treatment. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

On 06/[XXX]/2024 at 3:51pm, a WeRide vehicle (Car 1) safety driver in manual driving mode was attempting to make a u-turn at 6 mph on [XXX]. During the u-turn maneuver, a white chevy cruze (Car 2) traveling at 23 mph, having just made a right turn off of [XXX]., approached from behind on [XXX]. Car 2 steered left just before the impact but still clipped the front left side bumper of Car 1 with its (car2's) right side. The damage sustained to Car 1 was on the front bumper, left side, and the damage sustained to Car 2 was on the right passenger's door. Both parties pulled over to exchange information. Both vehicles involved in accident sustained moderate damage.
There were no injuries reported and no emergency responders were called.
During and 2 minutes before the incident, WeRide vehicle (Car 1) was in manual driving mode.

On July 9, 2025, Ford was notified by the driver of a Ford Explorer regarding an incident that occurred on July [XXX], 2025. While traveling northbound on Interstate [XXX], the vehicle struck a deer with Level 2 ADAS features Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) and Lane Centering Assist (LCA) engaged. According to the report, the vehicle experienced airbag deployment and was subsequently towed from the scene. No injuries were reported as a result of the incident.
Ford has confirmed that the vehicle involved was equipped with Co-Pilot360 Assist+, which includes ACC and LCA technologies. Ford has gained access to the vehicle and has retrieved both telematic and Event Data Recorder (EDR) data for further analysis. Ford is currently investigating whether these ADAS features were active at the time of the incident.

The customer contacted Honda Automobile Customer Service to discuss an unpaid balance on his totaled vehicle and requested to be connected with Honda Finance. When asked for details about the incident, the customer provided the following information.
On March [XXX], 2023, the customer was traveling at approximately 45 MPH on a curvy road with Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), Lane Keeping Assist System (LKAS), and Collision Mitigation Braking System (CMBS) engaged. The vehicle allegedly collided with a car parked illegally in a red zone. The customer reported that CMBS did not engage the brakes before the collision. ACC controlled the vehicles speed, and both ACC and LKAS were activated 20-30 minutes before the incident. No disengagements were reported. The weather was clear, and the customer did not notice any steering corrections from LKAS before the crash. Following the collision, the vehicles airbags deployed, though the customer could not recall which ones. The vehicle was towed from the scene, and the insurance company later declared it a total loss. No previous report updates apply, and no media sources were used.

The subject MY 2024 Mercedes-Benz CLE 300 4MATIC is equipped with L2 ADAS DISTRONIC Plus with Active Steering Assist and was being driven on [XXX], in the first left lane on [XXX] east on a gradual curve towards [XXX] in Washington State under wet roadway conditions. The driver alleged that "auto steering assistance" was engaged at approximately 70 mph and the car did not follow the lane markings and ended up on the shoulder.  The driver further alleged she immediately stepped on the brake and was "able to cancel the assist system and stopped the car at the shoulder side", resulting in tire/rim damage on the passenger side, and front bumper damage. The vehicle was towed to a local Mercedes-Benz dealership. The driver later alleged back pain and pain in both legs as a result of the crash.
On June 14, 2025, the driver provided additional information to the Mercedes-Benz Customer Care Center ("CCC") and alleged that distance assist, steering assist, and lane keeping assist were active at the time of the incident. In accordance with the requirements of the NHTSA ADAS SGO, MBUSA is submitting this 5-day incident report. 
This narrative summary is based entirely on the customer's description and allegations. MBUSA has not confirmed or verified this account or any of the customer's allegations and has initiated further investigation into the alleged incident.
8/15/2025 Update to 855-11157-1:
MBUSA conducted a vehicle inspection in June 2025. The inspection included a physical examination of the vehicle and system diagnostics and revealed that the EDR was not triggered. The information from the inspection was reviewed and analyzed in July and August 2025.  Based on the review, there was no indication of any Electronic Power Steering, Braking, or throttle control malfunctions. 
From its investigation and a review of the available data, MBUSA has concluded that the vehicle operated as intended. If MBUSA receives additional relevant information, it will update this report accordingly.

On December 2, 2024 at 10:54 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a plastic crate on East 3rd Street at South Central Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling westbound in the center lane on East 3rd Street, crossing the intersection with South Central Avenue when the front passenger side of the Waymo AV made contact with a plastic crate that was in the roadway within the Waymo AV’s lane of travel. The contact with the Waymo AV caused the crate to move into the adjacent right lane, which was occupied by a scooterist. The front tire of the scooter made contact with the crate and the scooter and scooterist fell. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Given the speed at which the scooter was traveling at the time of the contact, the scooter may have sustained damage.
